Definition: mixture, i.e. (specifically) wine mixed (with water or spices)
BiblicalUsage: mamçâk is wine mixed with water or spices, the kind of drink people linger over. In Proverbs 23:30 it marks those who tarry long at the wine and go to seek mixed wine, and in Isaiah 65:11 it stands on the table of those who forsake the LORD and furnish a drink offering to a false god. The same mixed cup can be a pleasure or an idol's offering.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mamçâk warns me that what I linger over shapes what I worship, and I hold that a drink shared at an idol's table is no small thing.
